summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare IP at install and import
details: The package is a stub shim under the internal-looking scope `@ecg-internal/*` whose only functional code is a host-metadata beacon. `package.json` declares a postinstall running `node beacon.cjs`, and `index.js` (the declared `main`) calls `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` at top level, so merely installing or requiring the package transmits a JSON payload containing the package name, hostname, install path, cwd, Node version, and user agent to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc` over plain HTTP. The exported value is a Proxy returning no-op stubs for any accessed property, which keeps bundlers and consumers from crashing while the beacon fires. The combination of an internal-sounding scope, a non-functional shim, dual install-time and import-time triggers, and callback to an unrelated hardcoded IP matches the dependency-confusion exfiltration pattern used to confirm successful intrusion into private build systems.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
